subject: Action: Order Form + DPA — geo-routing annex, SCCs alignment, and execution timeline
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver@datacove.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Suki Patel <suki.patel@datacove.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA + geo-routing annex — redlines attached

Connor — thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is our consolidated redline of the DPA (draft_DPA_v3_redlines.docx). Two items are gating for procurement here and we want to get to signature this month if possible:

1) Geo-routing / data residency commitments: we need a short annex that guarantees routing of EU customer traffic to EU-hosted capacity and a fallback path with explicit notification windows if routing changes are required.
2) SCCs + transfer carve-outs: request that SCCs be appended as an annex and that Redwood confirm the list of subprocessors + an SLA for notice prior to onboard (14 days).

We also noted the KMS statement in the MSA — can you confirm Redwood's KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed) and whether we can show that in the Order Form? Procurement expects a one-page summary to attach to their PO.

Attached: draft_DPA_v3_redlines.docx

Thanks,
Oliver Hayes
Head of Legal Operations
DataCove Inc.

Subject: Re: Draft DPA + geo-routing annex — redlines attached

Oliver — really appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Putting the internal team on this thread to get legal/ops/procurement alignment. Quick proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

- Today (Mon): Redwood legal to review redline and surface any non-starter language; Redwood infra to confirm geo-routing feasibility and KMS options.
- Tue: Redwood sends SCCs appendix + proposed Geo-Routing Annex language back to DataCove for a single pass.
- Wed-Fri: Procurement/Order Form tie-outs; finalize Order Form language for KMS and capacity.
- Next Tue: target DocuSign for Order Form + DPA (assuming no major new asks).

Laura / Ben / Aditya — can you each confirm acceptance of the timeline and own the bullets below?
- Laura: confirm the DPA redline is consistent with our SCCs approach and provide suggested wording for an SCCs Appendix + any required changes to the MSA indemnities. Also call out whether 14-day notice on subprocessors is acceptable or needs adjustment.
- Ben: own the Order Form language for KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed) and the commercial note for reserved EU capacity if DataCove wants to pin region. Add DocuSign link when ready.
- Aditya: infra feasibility — what are realistic constraints for geo-routing/failover windows and what ops notice do we need to provide customers?

Oliver / Suki — attaching the redline from your note here for internal reference. We will aim to return a tracked version of the DPA + a short 1-page annex for procurement.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver@datacove.com>, Suki Patel <suki.patel@datacove.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + geo-routing annex — redlines attached

Connor / team / Oliver — reviewed the draft_DPA_v3_redlines.docx. High-level summary and proposed edits below (inline follows in the tracked document we will send separately):

Summary:
- SCCs as an annex: acceptable. We should append a short "SCCs Appendix A" with the standard EU Commission language and a clarifying paragraph noting that the appendix incorporates the latest SCCs as of signature date. Add a cross-ref in the MSA that the DPA + SCCs govern transfers.
- Geo-Routing Annex: recommend framing this as a contractual "Geo-Routing Annex" that describes routing intent and the operational fallback (e.g., if EU capacity unavailable, Redwood may route via us-region with 48 hours' notice and an explanation; for emergency failover during a SEV, routing may change with immediate notice and after-action report). DataCove's requested 14-day notice for subprocessor onboards is aggressive; recommend 7 business days for standard onboards and 30 days for material subprocessor changes. We can offer 14 days as a middle ground for the initial 3 listed subprocessors.
- KMS: we can provide customer-managed KMS on Private deployments and offer Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted with encryption at rest and in transit. We will add an Order Form table showing which deployment options support customer-managed keys.
- Evidence: recommend we include a vendor-provided subprocessor snapshot (csv) and SOC2 report summary as attachments/links in the procurement packet.

Proposed concrete language (short extracts to include in the DPA):
- "Geo-Routing Annex: Redwood will, subject to capacity constraints, route Customer EU-origin traffic to EU-hosted capacity. In the event EU-hosted capacity is not available, Redwood shall notify Customer within 48 hours and route traffic to the nearest compatible region until EU capacity is restored.

- "SCCs Appendix A: The parties agree to incorporate by reference the EU Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses for Controller-Processor transfers (or other mechanism as agreed). The SCCs Appendix shall be included as an attachment to this DPA and updated by mutual written agreement."

Next steps: I will produce a tracked DPA with the SCCs Appendix + Geo-Routing Annex language and circulate before end of day. If DataCove accepts the 14-day interim subprocessor notice for the initially identified vendors, we can compress the timeline to target signature next week.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Oliver / Suki — thanks for your patience. Per Laura's notes, I've attached the SCCs appendix proposal (sccs_appendix_proposal.pdf) and a current subprocessor snapshot (subprocessor_snapshot.csv). Minor commercial notes: if DataCove wants reserved EU capacity pinned in the Order Form we will list the monthly commitment and associated unit rates (see attached one-pager). If not pinned, geo-routing will be a best-effort capability with the failover terms Laura outlined.

DocuSign & procurement cadence:
- I created a preliminary Order Form and placed it into DocuSign for your review: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ORDERFORM-DC-3571
- Procurement typically needs the one-page KMS / deployment matrix and the SCCs appendix to attach to their PO. Attached is a one-page KMS summary showing where customer-managed keys are available.

Next steps / ask list:
1) Oliver: confirm whether DataCove wants reserved EU capacity (yes/no) and whether the 14-day initial subprocessor notice is acceptable for the three vendors listed.
2) Connor / Aditya: confirm final ops notice windows and any implementation constraints so we can lock the Order Form controls.
3) Laura: I will push the tracked DPA + SCCs appendix into DocuSign once I get confirmation from DataCove on the two asks above (target: finish before 10 business days).

Attachments: sccs_appendix_proposal.pdf, subprocessor_snapshot.csv, KMS_deployment_matrix.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
